From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Melissa Tran <mtran@zenhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Amendment: Minimum guarantee + credit language

Grace / team — I reviewed the draft and ZenHealth's redlines. High-level legal points:

1) Terminology: prefer "Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC)" rather than "Usage Guarantee" — clearer for billing and audit.
2) Calculation: need explicit language for "billing month" boundaries and how credits are calculated when obligations aren't met. Recommend formula: (Committed MMC - Billed Usage) * committed rate, capped at X% of monthly invoice.
3) Preemptible capacity: we should allow exclusions for preemptible/spot instances but require that credits for interruptions to non-preemptible capacity are calculated against actual unavailability window.
4) Price protection: avoid open-ended price guarantees that extend beyond the contract term. Suggest a 12-month price lock clause tied to the MMC.

I've included line-by-line comments in a short text file attached (legal_comments_20261012.txt). Two items I need from ZenHealth to finalize wording: (a) confirm internal definition of "billed usage" (token vs unit); (b) whether they expect credits to settle as service credits or invoice adjustments.

If we can get those answers, I'll prepare a counter-redline and propose a DocuSign-ready amendment.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: legal_comments_20261012.txt]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Melissa Tran <mtran@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Amendment: Minimum guarantee + credit language

Melissa — quick follow up to Karthik's note with the clarifications we discussed internally:

- Billed usage: we will treat billed usage as billable inference tokens / embedding units as defined in the Order Form. We'll map any custom metering feeds before signature.
- Credits: we can offer service credits applied against the next invoice (not cash refunds).
- Cap on credits: commercial is comfortable with a 10% cap of the monthly invoice as an upper bound for service credits tied to unavailability (this keeps exposure predictable).
- Preemptible pools: we will exclude preemptible/spot capacity from the MMC and from SLA credit calculations (we will call these out explicitly in the SOW appendix).

Karthik will push a counter-redline today that incorporates MMC language and the 10% cap; Marissa will confirm the price-tier mapping for the MMC so ZenHealth knows which rate applies. Once ZenHealth signs off, we can prepare a DocuSign package.

Thanks —
Grace
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
